title: KYST | Five illustrated user stories
source: Real screenshots of the local application, using an isolated synthetic database.
assumptions: English explanations; original French application labels.
Two synthetic rooms, three conventional beds and six ambulatory places.
Eight pending requests and four confirmed bookings after the consultation example.
The multi-day preview simplifies room calendars and uses hypothetical execution factors.
After a calculation, some app forms reset their controls. Where shown with results, the submitted settings were re-entered for readability without rerunning or changing the results.

stories.title: Give a new patient two explained dates
stories.story: As a surgeon, I want room-time and length-of-stay estimates from the consultation details, so that I can discuss feasible dates with the patient.
stories.steps: Open Nouvelle demande; enter a pseudonym, birth year, sex, surgeon, diagnosis, CCAM code, procedure type and requested date window; choose Créer et proposer des dates.
stories.outcome: DEMO-NOUVEAU receives Monday 19 October and Friday 23 October. Each option explains room load, bed availability throughout the predicted stay, and the 10% vacation margin.
stories.check: The prediction is about 70 minutes and a four-day stay. A date proposal uses 71 rounded minutes. These are estimates of room occupancy, including more than the surgical act alone.
figures: Two possible dates with capacity explanations and the trained-model prediction.
extras: Consultation input form with synthetic details.

stories.title: Confirm a date and reserve the stay
stories.story: As a surgeon, I want to confirm one proposed date, so that the room capacity and beds for the predicted stay are reserved together.
stories.steps: Review Date A and select Confirmer cette date. Then open Lits to inspect the resulting occupancy forecast.
stories.outcome: The request becomes Programmée for 19 October, with a predicted last occupied day of 22 October. In this demo, conventional occupancy rises from one to two beds on those four days.
stories.check: Confirmation rechecks current capacity. A proposal by itself creates no reservation. Observed room time and stay can be recorded after surgery; recording them does not automatically retrain the models.
figures: The confirmed intervention, its predicted stay and fields for later observed outcomes.
extras: The Lits screen now shows 2/3 conventional beds occupied on 19-22 October.

stories.title: Plan a cohort, then publish proposals
stories.story: As a planner, I want to optimize pending requests together, so that shared room and bed constraints are considered across the cohort.
stories.steps: In Bloc, set 19-23 October under Optimisation de la cohorte; choose SMA x Metaheuristiques; calculate an overview, then select Publier des propositions.
stories.outcome: The combined engine places two of eight pending requests; six remain unassigned. Publication recalculates and checks capacity, then publishes two proposals awaiting clinical confirmation.
stories.check: Confirmed cases are preserved. Unassigned cases remain visible. Published proposals are still provisional and do not reserve beds or room time.
figures: Preview: two assignments and six unassigned requests.
Publication: two proposals, each awaiting clinical confirmation.

stories.title: Respond to a change in room availability
stories.story: As a planner, I want resource changes to trigger a review of pending proposals and highlight affected confirmed cases, so that the team can respond to a disruption.
stories.steps: In Ressources, deactivate Salle 1. Return to Bloc, inspect Interventions confirmées à revoir and select Actualiser les propositions.
stories.outcome: Four confirmed interventions are flagged because their room is unavailable. The refresh completes and updates two pending proposals; the queue returns to zero pending changes.
stories.check: Confirmed reservations remain in place for team review. The refresh does not automatically relocate confirmed operations. This demo uses manual refresh; a background worker is optional.
figures: The four affected confirmed interventions require review.
The completed refresh reports two updated proposals.

stories.title: Test the impact of longer hospital stays
stories.story: As a planner, I want to test a hypothetical scenario before changing the live plan, so that I can see whether beds or room capacity limit admissions.
stories.steps: Use Simulation Mesa : salles et lits for 19-23 October. Keep baseline, Réactive, room factor 1 and the 10:00-12:00 closure. Compare stay factor 1 with stay factor 2.
stories.outcome: With the same eight pending cases and four confirmed bookings, factor 1 starts two cases and leaves six unstarted. Factor 2 starts one and leaves seven unstarted. Both report zero bed-conflict days and zero solver failures.
stories.check: These are hypothetical execution durations derived from predictions. They are not observed patient outcomes, oracle forecasts, or a comparison proving that one solver is best. Simulation creates no bookings.
figures: Stay factor 1: two started; six unstarted; four replans.
Stay factor 2: one started; seven unstarted; two replans.
